experiences.title: PMA 153 • Rawalpindi AS&RC (second attempt, soldier's son)
experiences.summary: In his first attempt the essays were 'Drug addiction in educational institutes' and 'Our teachers'; he was asked about his father's rank and posting, abbreviations, seas, a percentage sum and an English debate on the war against terrorism. He answered only about 9 of 25 questions and once mixed an Urdu word into his English. In his second attempt the essays were 'The first time I faced rejection' and 'Loneliness is the best companion'. The Colonel kept offering speech topics until he could speak, and asked why he was not recommended before. In the second attempt 16 of 20 candidates were recommended.
asked: What are you doing now?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
If you are so passionate, why did you not apply in earlier courses?
Where is your father now? What is his rank?
What are the full forms of AFIC and JCO?
Where are the Yellow Sea, the Dead Sea and the Black Sea?
A percentage maths question.
Speak in English on the war against terrorism.
Why did you study in a private school?
Why were you not recommended in your previous interview?
What is the full form of ATM?
Speak on co-education, the education system of Pakistan or the impact of urbanisation.
tips: You can be recommended even if you do not know many GK answers.
Speak fully in English; do not mix Urdu words.
Prepare a few common speech topics so you are not nervous when asked to speak.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar centre (Hafiz, economics student)
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on whether college students should choose their own subjects and an Urdu essay on new technology making people lazy. The Colonel asked how many times he had applied and why he changed his centre. He could not explain the difference between a credit and a debit card even though he studies economics, and kept saying sorry. Because he wrote that he is a Hafiz, the psychologist asked Islamic questions, including the meaning of a Quran word, which he could not answer. He was not recommended.
asked: What are you doing these days?
How many times have you applied for army tests?
Why did you change your test centre?
What is the difference between a credit card and a debit card?
What do you know about fighter pilots?
What do you think about travelling by train?
What is democracy?
Are you a Hafiz-e-Quran?
What is the meaning of 'Wal-yatalattaf', the middle word of the Quran?
What was the real name of Hazrat Abu Bakr (RA)?
After how many years did Hazrat Yusuf (AS) meet his father?
tips: Know the basics of your own subject; failing an easy question from your own field hurts a lot.
If you write that you are a Hafiz, expect Quran questions and learn the meaning of what you memorised.
Saying 'sorry' again and again gives a bad impression; prepare well.
Have a clear reason ready if you changed your centre or applied many times.

experiences.title: PMA 154 • Multan AS&RC (pre-engineering, 90% marks)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Effects of the internet' (English) and 'The secret of success' (Urdu). Because he had 90% in FSc pre-engineering, the Colonel asked many maths questions on triangles and angles. He made a mistake and got confused but did not lose confidence. He had written 'watching movies' as a hobby, so he was asked which movies and the latest one. The psychologist told him to come out of movies and play sports, because his physical test marks were low.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is a right triangle? What are the types of triangles?
What is an equilateral triangle and what are its angles?
What is an acute angle and an acute-angled triangle?
What is an obtuse angle and an obtuse-angled triangle?
What does your father do?
What are your hobbies and interests?
What kind of movies do you watch? What is the latest Avengers movie?
What is Ohm's law?
Why are your physical test marks low?
tips: If you have high marks in a subject, expect deep questions from it.
Be ready to answer in detail about anything you write in your form, like hobbies.
If you make a mistake, say sorry and keep your confidence.
Take part in sports and outdoor activities; it shows in your profile.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Swat area candidate
experiences.summary: A Colonel took the interview. He asked what the candidate is doing these days and why he chose the Army when there are thousands of other jobs. He asked about the current situation in Swat and how militants get food and shelter. Then he switched the interview to English and asked basic grammar questions. He also asked why the candidate did not choose medicine after good FSc pre-medical marks, and why he wrote video games as a hobby.
asked: How do you pronounce your name?
What are you doing these days?
Why did you choose the Pak Army when there are thousands of other jobs?
What is the situation in Swat right now?
From where do the Taliban get their food, shelter and water?
What is the national language of Pakistan?
What is the official language of Pakistan?
What is the currency of Afghanistan?
What is active voice and passive voice?
What is a noun and what is a verb?
You got good marks in FSc pre-medical, so why did you not choose medicine?
Why did you write playing video games as your hobby?
tips: Know the latest news about your own home area.
Be ready for the officer to switch from Urdu to English.
Be ready to explain every hobby you write in your form.
If you do not know an answer, simply say 'Sorry sir, I don't know'.

experiences.title: PMA • Faisalabad AS&RC (long pressure interview)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'The person I hate the most' and 'My family'. His interview was longer than usual because he stayed confident even when he did not know answers, so the Colonel kept testing him. He was pressed on details like the tehsils of Sargodha and the status of Islamabad. At the end the Colonel asked why he should or should not be recommended.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What does 'N.B.' in your village address mean, and why is it called that?
How many tehsils does Sargodha have? Name them.
A dozen eggs cost Rs 300. What is the price of one egg?
A train moves at 110 km/h. How far will it go in 2.5 hours?
Which team is touring Pakistan these days? In which continent is it?
Who won the FIFA World Cup? In which continent is that country?
What is the capital of Germany?
What is the capital of Balochistan? Name two more cities of Balochistan.
Where is PMA, and in which province?
In which province is Islamabad?
If I recommend you, why? If I do not recommend you, why?
tips: Do not guess wildly; the officer dislikes made-up answers.
Know the facts about your own home area.
The officer may pressure you on purpose; stay calm.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Rawalpindi centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English and an Urdu essay before the interview. The board was a Lieutenant Colonel and a female psychologist Major. He knocked, asked permission, greeted, sat straight and kept eye contact. The Colonel asked about his area, his father's job, his old schools and boarding-school life, then told him to speak for 2 minutes on hostel life, followed by a few quick GK questions. The psychologist asked nothing.
asked: Which area are you from?
What does your father do and where is he posted?
Tell us about your previous schools and colleges.
Speak for 2 minutes on the impact of hostel life.
What is the full form of OGRA?
What is the currency of Bangladesh?
What is the currency of Iran?
What is the currency of Gilgit-Baltistan? (trick question)
Who is the Governor of Punjab?
What is 5% of 500?
tips: Knock, ask permission, greet with Assalam-o-Alaikum and sit only when told.
Sit straight, do not cross your legs or lock your hands, and look the interviewer in the eye.
Confidence and body language matter more than the number of right answers.
Learn currencies, capitals, and the names of the President, PM, Chief Ministers and Governors.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Faisalabad centre
experiences.summary: A Lieutenant Colonel and a Captain took the interview. After his introduction, the Lt Col asked about his father, siblings, three strengths, three weaknesses and his plan B. Because he said he had no interest in football, he was tested on current sports news like the FIFA World Cup and a cricket series in Pakistan. The Captain then asked questions from his bio data form. He was nervous at first, but the panel made him comfortable.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your father.
Do you have any siblings? What are their names and what do they do?
Tell me three strengths of yours.
Tell me three weaknesses of yours.
What is your plan B?
Are you interested in football? Where is the FIFA World Cup being held?
What is the capital of that country?
Which teams reached the World Cup semi-final?
Which foreign cricket team is touring Pakistan now, and what was the last match result?
Questions from your bio data form
tips: Follow current news, including big sports events, even if they are not your hobby.
Prepare three strengths and three weaknesses in advance.
Nervousness usually goes away after the first few questions, so keep going calmly.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Lt Col and Major board
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on co-education and an Urdu essay on local tourism (another report of the same board lists 'My father' and 'Is money everything for a person?'). The Lieutenant Colonel asked about his qualification, father's job and family, and even personal and honesty questions. The Major asked about his hobbies and brothers, and then he was asked why he wants to join the Army. He could not answer five GK questions, so the Lt Col told him to improve his GK, but he was still recommended.
asked: What is your qualification?
Tell me about your father and family.
Do you have a girlfriend?
What are your hobbies?
Tell me about your brothers.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Have you ever watched restricted websites?
Do you tell lies?
Five general knowledge questions
tips: Answer personal and honesty questions truthfully and calmly.
Prepare general knowledge well, because weak GK is noticed.
Take permission before sitting.
Leave properly: stand up, thank them, say salam and walk out calmly.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Quetta centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on 'A wealthy life is better than a peaceful life' and an Urdu essay on the role of teacher, student and parents in education. A Lieutenant Colonel and a Major asked about his district, his college and why he wants to join the Army. When asked about the Indus civilization, he honestly said he is weak in Pakistan Studies and asked for science questions, and the panel agreed. The Major also asked why he did not go for MDCAT, about his time as house prefect, and what big thing he wants to do for his family, province and country.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your district.
Tell me about your college.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
What is the Indus civilization?
What are algae, fungi, chromosomes, ions and ionic bonds?
What is Newton's second law and its equation?
Your favourite subject is biology, so why did you not appear in the MDCAT?
You were a house prefect. Tell me about leadership at your level.
What big thing do you want to do for your family, your province and the people of Pakistan?
tips: If you are weak in one area, say so honestly and offer your strong subject; the panel may accept it.
Be ready to explain any leadership role (like prefect) written in your form.
Prepare a clear answer for why you chose the Army over other careers.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • South Waziristan candidate
experiences.summary: He wrote 'Knowledge is power' in English and the importance of religion in human life in Urdu. A Colonel asked where he is from, where he lives now, and about his education and siblings. A Major then asked general knowledge questions, and he politely said sorry for one he did not know. At the end the Colonel asked how he thought his interview went and wished him luck.
asked: Where are you from, and where are you settled now?
Introduce yourself.
Tell me about your education.
Tell me about your siblings.
Who was the first President of the USA?
What is the capital of Australia?
Which metal is found in liquid form at room temperature?
Name the rivers of KPK.
What is GPS?
What are the official and national languages of Pakistan and India?
How do you think your interview went?
tips: Ask permission before sitting down and keep eye contact.
GK alone does not decide the result; show confidence but do not be overconfident.
If you do not know an answer, politely say sorry.

experiences.title: PMA • Jhelum candidate (weak GK)
experiences.summary: His English essay was 'Why I want to join the Pak Army as an officer' and his Urdu essay was 'How can we serve humanity'. The Colonel asked him to introduce himself, then asked about his father's business and said he should have mentioned it in the introduction. Many GK and Islamiat questions followed and he could not answer most of them, so the Colonel said his general knowledge was very weak. At the end he asked simple physics and science questions about things in the room.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What does your father do? What kind of business is it?
Where do you live?
How many rivers are in Punjab? What does 'Punjab' mean?
Name the mountain ranges of Pakistan.
In which Hijri year did the event of Karbala happen?
When did fasting become compulsory?
Which countries fought in World War 2?
Which river flows near Kohat, and which river is near Karachi?
State Ohm's law. What does resistance mean?
State Pythagoras theorem.
What is this window made of? What is this scale made of?
tips: Mention your father's job and other key facts in your introduction so the officer does not have to ask.
Prepare basic GK: rivers, mountain ranges and Islamic history dates.
Revise basic physics and maths laws from your FSc.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Faisalabad AS&RC (repeat attempt, far centre)
experiences.summary: He first wrote one English and one Urdu essay. In the room the questions were easy and mostly general. He was asked about himself, why he failed his previous attempt, why he chose a far test centre, and some Pakistan geography such as dams, rivers and the constitution. He was also asked to talk about his home town for two minutes without stopping.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Why did you fail in your previous course?
Why did you come to this centre when other centres were closer to you?
Tell us about the Constitution of Pakistan.
Tell us about the dams of Pakistan.
Tell us about the rivers of Pakistan. Which is the longest river?
Speak about your home town for 2 minutes without stopping.
What is the most regretful day of your life?
Which places have you visited in this city?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Tell us about the continents.
Tell us about your family background and your friends.
tips: Be ready to explain why you failed in a past attempt.
Prepare a 2-minute talk about your own city or district.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar AS&RC (step-family questions)
experiences.summary: He said 'May I come in, sir?' and the Colonel pointed out that a lady was also on the panel, so he should say 'sir and madam'. He was asked about his siblings, his step-mother and step-brother, and he knew very little about them, which the psychologist did not like. He answered questions on the Indus Waters Treaty and the UNO too briefly. He was told he was not recommended and to work harder; he said he would improve his communication, English and knowledge about his family.
asked: Why did you only say 'sir' when a lady is also on the panel?
Introduce yourself.
How many siblings do you have?
What do you know about your step-mother and step-brother?
Why did your parents separate?
Explain the Indus Waters Treaty.
Define the UNO.
What will you improve before your next attempt?
tips: Look at the whole panel when you enter; if a lady officer is present, greet 'sir' and 'madam'.
Know full details about your whole family, including step-family, and fill the form completely.
Give full answers; very short answers make a weak impression.
The panel watches your body language and the tone of your voice.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (serving PAF airman)
experiences.summary: About 150 boys came and his turn came around 1 pm. The Colonel was busy, so a female psychologist Major took the interview. She asked why he wanted to switch from the PAF to the Army, a speech on globalization, and many quick GK and Islamiat questions.
asked: Are you serving in the PAF? Why do you want to switch from the PAF to the Army?
Speak on globalization and its impacts.
What is the capital of Ireland?
What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
Who was the first recipient of the Nishan-e-Haider?
How many surahs are in the Quran? How many are Makki?
What are the full forms of CNG and NEPRA?
Who is the Governor of Sindh?
Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh?
What is 3% of 40?
tips: Be confident and keep eye contact.
Your appearance matters, even if your clothes are not costly.
Stay calm and think for 3-4 seconds before answering.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Multan centre
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on unemployment and an Urdu essay on the qualities of a good student. He asked permission to enter, stood beside the chair and sat only when told. The Colonel asked him to introduce himself, then asked biology questions and questions on Pakistan's constitutions. The psychologist asked what he would do if not recommended and who Edhi was. He left politely with a smile.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What are the longest and smallest bones of the human body?
What are the types of blood cells?
What is the difference between a plant cell and an animal cell?
Who was the first President of Pakistan?
How many constitutions has Pakistan had?
What is the difference between the 1962 and 1973 constitutions?
If we do not recommend you, what will you do?
Who was Abdul Sattar Edhi?
tips: Ask 'May I come in, sir?', stand beside the chair and sit only when told.
Revise the basics of your FSc subjects, because the Colonel may ask from them.
End with a polite thank you and salam.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (pre-medical candidate)
experiences.summary: Candidates reached early in the morning and wrote an English and an Urdu essay, about 10 minutes each. Later they were lined up and called one by one on a bell. A Colonel and a psychologist took the interview. He was asked to speak on education and co-education and why he left medicine for the Army. The result came about 30-35 minutes after the whole batch finished.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Speak on the downfall of the education system.
Why are you not going into medicine when you did pre-medical in FSc?
Speak on co-education.
What is the capital of Norway?
Speak on 'My Pakistan' in Urdu.
Some percentage questions.
What is your elder brother doing?
What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
Why only the Army and not the Navy or Air Force?
tips: Expect about 10 minutes for each essay.
Be ready to explain why you chose the Army over your field of study.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Karachi centre
experiences.summary: Only 4 out of 25 candidates were selected that day. The officer asked the meaning of his name, asked him to introduce himself, and asked why his grades were so low. He honestly said it was his own fault because he gave more time to sports, and he did not blame his school or college. The officer then asked quick estimation questions and talked about his sports for 3-4 minutes. He believes neat dress, eye contact, a smile and fluent English got him easy questions while others got hard geography questions.
asked: What is the meaning of your name?
Please introduce yourself.
Your grades are very low. Why?
If I ask you to go and touch the Arabian Sea and come back, how much time will it take?
What is the length and width of the table in front of me? Show me.
Which sports do you play? (detailed questions on sports)
tips: If your marks are low, accept it honestly; do not blame your school, college or anyone else.
Keep eye contact and a natural smile throughout the interview.
Wear a light-coloured full-sleeve formal shirt (sleeves not folded), dark dress pants and formal lace-up shoes; no jeans or loafers.
Be ready for practical estimation questions like distance, time or the size of an object.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (name and maps)
experiences.summary: About 55 candidates came that day and he was second last, so he waited a long time. A Colonel and a psychologist Major took the interview. They asked the meaning of his name, his marks, why he wants to join the Army, and some map and Army questions. The interview lasted only a few minutes, and only 8 or 9 out of 55 were selected.
asked: What is the meaning of your name?
What were your matric and FSc marks?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Where are Asia and Europe on the map?
Where are Russia and Greenland on the world map?
What is the budget of the Pakistan Army?
What are the ranks of non-commissioned officers in the Army?
tips: Be ready for a long wait; stay fresh and calm.
Speak loudly and clearly, and keep your hands and feet still.
Know Army ranks and have a rough idea of the defence budget.
Most candidates fail because they lose confidence, not because of hard questions.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • D.I. Khan AS&RC (serving soldier)
experiences.summary: The panel was a Colonel and a psychologist Major. The Colonel asked about his serving unit, where it is now, and where he belongs. The psychologist asked history questions about 1905, 1906 and 1911 and the capital of AJK. Then he was asked about his family members, his FA studies and their scope, why he had not prepared for the interview, and finally his current rank.
asked: Where have you come from?
Which unit are you serving in? Where is your unit now?
Where do you belong to?
What is the capital of Azad Kashmir?
Why is 1905 important? Why 1906? Why 1911?
What do your family members do?
You did FA. What is its scope? Tell us about your academic career.
Why did you not prepare yourself for the interview?
What is your current rank?
tips: Serving soldiers should be ready for questions about their unit and rank.
Answer family questions boldly.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Karachi AS&RC (FSc marks lower than matric)
experiences.summary: He wrote an English essay on 'Me after 10 years' and an Urdu essay on happiness and sorrow. A Lieutenant Colonel asked about his father's job, his three elder brothers, and why his FSc marks were lower than his matric marks. He was given a topic to speak on. A lady psychologist then asked a few GK questions; he did not know one and said sorry confidently.
asked: Are you from Islamabad?
What does your father do?
You have three elder brothers. What do they do?
Why are your FSc marks lower than your matric marks?
Speak on 'Single curriculum in the whole country'.
What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
Who is the Prime Minister of New Zealand?
In which year was the Objectives Resolution passed?
What was the old name of Madina?
tips: Be confident and natural; show them who you really are.
If you do not know an answer, say 'Sorry sir/madam' calmly and confidently.

experiences.title: PMA 154 • University student (speech topic changed)
experiences.summary: The Colonel asked how he was, what he was doing and which university he studies at. He was then given speaking topics one after another: impact of globalization, religious harmony and gender equality. He was asked if he had memorised these topics, and he honestly said no. The female psychologist asked an Islamiat question and a percentage sum.
asked: How are you? What are you doing nowadays?
Are you a university student? Which university?
Speak on the impact of globalization.
Speak on religious harmony.
Speak on gender equality.
Did you learn these topics by heart?
What is the capital of Sweden?
On which prophet was the Zaboor revealed?
What is 3% of 300?
tips: Be ready for the topic to change suddenly; keep speaking.
Practise speaking on common social topics without memorising.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Peshawar centre (second attempt)
experiences.summary: He was not recommended in the PMA 150 initial interview and tried again. He wrote an English essay on the role of parents in raising children and an Urdu essay on hard work and good luck. The Lieutenant Colonel asked where Russia is and why he was not recommended last time. The Major asked about current office holders and asked him to show Russia on a map. He took a moment to think, answered calmly, and passed.
asked: What is your name?
Where is Russia?
Why were you not recommended in your last initial interview?
Who is the Chairman Senate?
Who is the Speaker of the National Assembly?
Who was the previous President of Pakistan, and where is he now?
Do you know how to read a map? Show Russia on the map.
tips: If you failed before, explain honestly why and what you have improved.
Practise finding countries on a world map.
Know current office holders like the Chairman Senate, NA Speaker and the previous President.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (GK and Islamic history)
experiences.summary: After the introduction, the interviewer asked mostly general knowledge and Islamic history questions. He was asked about Indian cities, US states, Pakistan-India wars and NATO. He could not answer some questions, like the main enemy in Ghazwa-e-Khandaq, but he still passed. He was also asked whether any relative serves in the Army.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Name 5 cities of India.
Name 5 states of the USA.
How many wars have been fought between Pakistan and India, and when?
What is NATO?
Who are the Azwaj-e-Mutahharat (wives of the Holy Prophet PBUH)?
Who is called Saifullah?
In which Hijri year was Ghazwa-e-Khandaq fought, and who was the main enemy?
Do you have any relative serving in the Army?
tips: You can pass even if you cannot answer every GK question.
Revise Pakistan-India wars, NATO and the main battles of Islamic history.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • GK and science questions
experiences.summary: After a self-introduction, the interviewer moved to general knowledge, history, science and simple maths. Questions covered Pakistan's provinces, cities and neighbours, World War 2, democracy and the Two Nation Theory. He was also asked intermediate science, like Mendel's laws, and a train speed problem.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is democracy?
Explain World War 2.
Where is gold found in Pakistan?
What are Mendel's laws?
What is the difference between organic and inorganic compounds?
Name four cities of Sindh.
How many provinces does Pakistan have? Name them.
Name the neighbouring countries of Pakistan.
A train moving at 60 km/h takes 120 seconds to pass through a tunnel. How long is the tunnel? (ignore the train's length)
What is the Two Nation Theory?
tips: Revise your intermediate science subjects, because basic concept questions are asked.
Practise simple speed, time and distance sums in your head.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (quick GK and Islamiat)
experiences.summary: Only the female psychologist took his interview. His essays were 'Me after 10 years' and 'Deeds make life heaven or hell'. She asked many quick GK and Islamiat questions and two short speeches, interrupting after a few lines.
asked: What is your name and your father's name?
What are you doing these days?
When was the Objectives Resolution passed?
What is the capital of Sudan?
What is the currency of South Africa?
Who is the Vice President of the USA?
How many surahs are in the Quran? How many are Madni?
Speak on how social media affects youth.
Speak on gender equality.
What are the full forms of PEMRA and OGRA?
What is 4% of 1100?
tips: Short speeches may be stopped after a few lines; make your main point first.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (speech)
experiences.summary: He had to give a speech on why Pakistan's education system is declining. The psychologist asked him about 10 GK questions and he could answer only 4 or 5, saying sorry for the rest. The two written essays carried 20 marks (10 English, 10 Urdu) and he did them well. He believes his good essays and confident speech got him recommended even though his GK was weak.
asked: Give a speech on the reasons behind the decline of the education system in Pakistan.
What is the currency of Turkey?
Where is the White Sea?
Where is the Yellow Sea?
Who is the Chief Minister of Balochistan?
What is 5% of 700?
What was the old name of Makkah?
tips: The written essays carry about 20 marks (10 English, 10 Urdu), so practise both.
A good speech and good essays can make up for weak GK answers.
Keep current affairs updated, like the names of Chief Ministers.

experiences.title: PMA • Multan AS&RC (D.G. Khan, geography)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Value of time' and 'Who is responsible for unemployment in society'. The Colonel asked why his FSc marks were 10% lower and many geography questions on rivers, Trimmu, mountain ranges and motorways; he did not know many. As a pre-engineering student he was also asked about types of triangles. The psychologist observed him and checked his essay.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Why are your FSc marks 10% lower?
Name the rivers of Punjab. Where do they join? Have you heard of Trimmu?
Name the mountain ranges. Which range is near D.G. Khan?
Which provinces does the Sulaiman Range touch?
Where are the Kirthar Range and the Hindu Kush?
Which motorway goes near D.G. Khan? Name the motorways of Pakistan.
How many types of triangles are there by angles? What is an acute triangle?
tips: Know the geography around your own district.
Smile and stay confident.

experiences.title: PMA 154 • Lahore AS&RC (lady psychologist only)
experiences.summary: Only a female psychologist took his interview. She asked what he was doing (MDCAT), why he wants to join the Army, and several GK questions. He answered 8 out of 10, and even gave one wrong answer with full confidence. He spoke for about half a minute on co-education. His essays were 'A friend in need is a friend indeed' and 'The bitter truth of my life'.
asked: What are you doing nowadays?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
When was the Objectives Resolution passed?
What is the capital of Sudan?
Who is the Prime Minister of the UK?
What does CNG stand for?
Who is the Governor of Sindh?
Speak on the benefits of co-education.
tips: Stay confident even if you are not sure of an answer.
Keep current office holders (PMs, governors) up to date.

experiences.title: PMA • Peshawar AS&RC (map with laser pointer)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Gender discrimination is a myth' (English) and 'Freedom of expression' (Urdu). The Colonel asked basic personal questions, gave him a speech on improving education, an Urdu-to-English translation and questions on military ranks. The psychologist asked him to find places on a world map with a laser pointer.
asked: What is your name? How are you?
What are you doing here? Why are you not studying?
Speak on how to improve our education system.
Translate into English: 'Yeh sarak Lahore jati hai.'

Tell the ranks of non-commissioned and commissioned officers.

Show the Caribbean Sea, Moscow, Russia and Greenland on the map.

Learn Army ranks and their correct spellings.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Rawalpindi centre (psychologist first)
experiences.summary: He wrote an Urdu essay on the importance of law in society and an English essay on 'Money or Wisdom'. At first only the lady psychologist was in the room, and later a Colonel came in. She asked him to introduce himself, why he wants to join the Army, and some GK questions. He politely said 'Sorry madam' for the ones he did not know. At the end he spoke for 2 minutes on 'Armed Forces'.

Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Who is the President of Russia?
What is the full form of FATA?
What was the old name of Faisalabad?
Speak for 2 minutes on the topic 'Armed Forces'.

They mainly check your confidence and the way you talk.
If you do not know an answer, say sorry politely instead of guessing.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (not recommended)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Social media and its impact' and 'Problems of unemployment'. The Colonel left the room, so the psychologist took the interview. She asked about his education, several GK questions he could not answer, and a speech on overpopulation. He felt he did well but was not recommended.

What are the weaknesses of our education system?
What is the smallest country in Asia?
Who designed Pakistan's flag?
How long does the national anthem take to play?
What is 4% of 900?
Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh? What is the currency of Turkey?
Speak on overpopulation.

Feeling the interview went well does not guarantee a result; prepare GK too.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (three speech topics)
experiences.summary: Only the psychologist took his interview. His essays were 'Poverty and its effects' and 'Even when I did not want to...'. She gave him three speech topics and many GK questions.

Speak on 'Unemployment leads to crime'.
Speak on globalization.
Speak on the benefits of western culture.
What was the old name of Makkah?

Who is the Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee?

experiences.title: PMA 154 • MDCAT student (one weakness to remove)
experiences.summary: His essays included 'Importance of tourism' and 'Meaning and purpose of education'. The Colonel asked for an introduction and whether he had applied for MBBS, since he had taken the MDCAT. He was asked about his elder brothers and some geography. The Major asked which one weakness he would remove first; he said offering all five prayers regularly. He was also asked if he had a girlfriend.

Have you applied for MBBS?
Tell me about your elder brothers.
Where is the Khojak Pass, and which places does it connect?
What lies to the south of India?

Do you have a girlfriend?

Know one honest weakness and how you are working on it.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (149 candidates)
experiences.summary: 149 candidates came; he wrote the essays first and waited about four hours. A Lieutenant Colonel and a female psychologist interviewed him, and the psychologist kept writing notes. He was asked about his family from the bio data, why he wants the Army, a two-minute speech, GK and Islamiat. His essays were 'Me after ten years' and 'Deeds make life heaven or hell'.
asked: How are you?
Personal and family questions from the bio data form.
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Speak for 2 minutes on the impact of education on youth.
What is the capital of Ireland?
What was the age of the Holy Prophet (PBUH) when he passed away?
How many Muslims were martyred in the Battle of Badr?
tips: Be confident, keep eye contact and dress well.
Greet both officers when you leave.

experiences.title: PMA • Lahore AS&RC (three weaknesses and fear)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Devolution of power in Pakistan' and 'An event that changed my life'. He closed the door gently and greeted. The Colonel read his form and asked about his family, his three weak points and his low intermediate marks. The psychologist Major asked what fear he has.

Tell me your three weaknesses.
Why is your intermediate percentage low compared to matric?
How much of Pakistan's area is Balochistan?
Which country is to the east of India?
What fear do you have?
tips: Be confident and keep good eye contact.
Keep a good tone and do not speak in a shaky voice.
Close the door gently when you enter.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (many short GK questions)
experiences.summary: Only the psychologist was in the room. His essays were 'Unpleasant event of my life' and 'There was a time in my life when I...'. He was asked many short GK questions and a speech on gender equality.
asked: What are the full forms of CNG and FATF?
Which mountain range lies between Pakistan and Afghanistan?
Where is the M-5 motorway?
What is the currency of South Africa?
Who are the Prime Ministers of India and New Zealand?
Who is the Governor of Punjab?
What is 3% of 500?
Speak on gender equality.
tips: Keep eye contact however many questions you are asked.
If you do not know, say 'Sorry sir' with full confidence.

experiences.title: PMA • Faisalabad AS&RC (glasses in form photo)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Unforgettable incident of my life' (English) and 'My family' (Urdu). The Colonel asked why he was not wearing glasses in his bio data photo. He got nervous and named a Balochistan city when asked for KPK cities. He said his hobby was internet scrolling, which surprised the Colonel. He then answered a geography question and a speed-distance sum correctly and left on a good note.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Since when do you wear glasses? Why are you not wearing them in your form photo?
What are the capitals of Balochistan and KPK?
Name five cities of KPK other than Peshawar.
What are your hobbies? Which games do you play?
Which country is to the east of Iran?
A car moves at 110 km/h. How far will it go in 2.5 hours?
tips: Choose a sensible hobby; 'internet scrolling' gives a bad impression.
Make sure your form photo matches how you look now.
Do not panic; a calm second answer is better than a wrong rushed one.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Rawalpindi AS&RC (father retired from Army)
experiences.summary: His essays were about an unpleasant event (English) and 'A time came in my life when...' (Urdu). A female psychologist and a Colonel interviewed him. He was asked to speak on tourism and some quick GK and percentage questions. They also asked about his retired father's unit and service.
asked: What are you doing nowadays?
Speak on tourism.
What is the currency of Denmark?
Who is the Prime Minister of Bangladesh?
How many Makki surahs are there?
What is 3% of 500?
Your father is retired from the Army. Which unit was he in?
tips: If your father served in the Army, know his unit and service details.
Stay cool and relaxed.

experiences.title: PMA • Peshawar AS&RC (BS English student)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Imagination is more powerful than knowledge' (English) and 'Education system in Pakistan' (Urdu). A Lieutenant Colonel and a Major were present, and the Major looked at him from head to toe. He was asked about his studies and why his home and university were in different districts. When asked why the ISSB did not recommend him earlier, he answered honestly. 19 out of 39 were recommended.
asked: What is your name?
What are you doing nowadays apart from PMA?
Where are you from, and where do you study?
Why were you not recommended by the ISSB?
How many brothers and sisters do you have?
Are you still interested in joining PMA?
tips: Stay confident.
Answer honestly about past failures.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Multan AS&RC (CA student)
experiences.summary: His English essay was 'I want to join the Pakistan Army as an officer because...' and his Urdu essay was 'The best way to help people'. He introduced himself in English. Because he was studying Chartered Accountancy, the Colonel asked him accounting questions, then GK on mountain passes, rivers and capitals. The psychologist asked why his physical and academic marks were low even after many attempts.

What are the accounting entries for assets, losses, profit and expenses?
What is a pass? Name the passes of Pakistan.
Name the rivers of Punjab.
What are the capitals of Turkey, Iran, Qatar and the Netherlands?
Why are your physical and academic marks low even after many attempts?
tips: Expect questions from the subject you are studying now.
If you have many attempts, be ready to explain your weak marks honestly.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Lahore AS&RC (moral values and culture)
experiences.summary: He wrote one Urdu and one English essay first. The panel asked his name, family background and an introduction. Then they asked him to explain moral values and culture with examples, and why he wants to join the Army. He did not know the capital of Finland and simply said sorry, but answered the capital of Norway.
asked: What is your name? Are you fine?
What is your family background?
Introduce yourself.
Explain moral values: where do they come from? Give an example.
What is culture?
Why do you want to join the Army?
What is the capital of Finland?
What is the capital of Norway?
tips: Answer concept questions in your own words, with a simple example.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Lahore AS&RC (psychologist only watched)
experiences.summary: His essays were on poor economic progress (Urdu) and 'How we can help others' (English). The Colonel confirmed his name and district, asked about his college and why he chose it, and what he was doing now. He asked a quick percentage question and why he wants to join the Army. He did not know where the Bay of Bengal is. The psychologist asked nothing and only watched him.
asked: You are from (your district)?
Which college did you study in, and why did you go there?
What are you doing nowadays?
What is 2% of 400?
Why do you want to join the Army?
Where is the Bay of Bengal?
tips: Be confident from the first moment and keep your voice steady.
Even if the psychologist asks nothing, they are observing you the whole time.

experiences.title: PMA • Peshawar AS&RC (arts student, current affairs)
experiences.summary: After basic questions about his address, the officers asked detailed current affairs questions because he had studied arts. Topics included Kashmir, Israel-Palestine, Armenia-Azerbaijan, Russia-Ukraine and Pakistan's political and economic problems. He had a good discussion and they even thanked him. He felt confidence and communication mattered more than talent.
asked: Where do you live now, and why do you live there?
What do you know about the Kashmir issue?
What do you know about the Israel-Palestine war?
What do you know about the Armenia-Azerbaijan conflict?
What do you know about the Russia-Ukraine war?
How are political instability and the economic crisis affecting Pakistan?
tips: Confidence, communication and attitude matter more than knowledge.
If you are an arts student, keep your current affairs strong.

experiences.title: PMA • Lahore AS&RC (fear of deep water)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Good and bad parents' (English) and 'Loneliness is the best companion' (Urdu). The Colonel asked about his name, family and three weaknesses. He was asked about the fear of deep water he wrote in his form and whether he plans to learn swimming. The psychologist gave him a life-jacket situation with a friend.
asked: What is your name, and what does it mean?
What is your father's name and occupation?
Tell me about your siblings.
Tell me three of your weaknesses.
Your biggest fear is deep water. Why? Do you know swimming? Will you learn?
You and your friend are drowning and there is only one life jacket. Who gets it, and why?
tips: Anything you write in the form, like your fears, can be asked; be ready to explain.
Be confident and keep good eye contact.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (applied for PAF airman)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Unforgettable event of my life' and 'National language is the base of progress'. His debate topic was 'Wealth is better than knowledge'. The Lieutenant Colonel asked why he had applied for PAF airman and why he wants the Army.
asked: How are you? What are you doing nowadays?
Why did you apply for PAF airman?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Debate: wealth is better than knowledge.
What is the capital of Greece?
What is the full form of UNICEF?
Who is the Chairman Senate?
Who is the President of India?
tips: Confidence, eye contact and trust in Allah and yourself.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (female candidate)
experiences.summary: Her essays were on Iqbal's Shaheen and the impact of social media on moral values. She stood by the chair until told to sit. The officer asked about her surname, asked her to describe Islamophobia, and asked map questions about Moscow. He also asked her height in inches, her district and where she was doing her BS.

Describe Islamophobia.
Where is Moscow, and in which continent is it?
What is your height in inches?
Which is your district?
Where are you doing your BS?
tips: Know your height in inches and other personal details exactly.
Learn the map locations of major world capitals.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (standing on right side)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Life is not a bed of roses' and 'My dream'. A lady psychologist and a Lieutenant Colonel were present. He stood on the right side of the chair and was asked why. He was given a speech on the falling standard of education and some GK, and he got a percentage sum wrong.
asked: Why did you stand on the right side of the chair?
Speak on the falling standard of education in Pakistan.
What are you doing nowadays? Why have you not taken admission yet?
What is the capital of Ireland?
Who are the President and Prime Minister of Azad Kashmir?
What is 5% of 400?
tips: Confidence and eye contact matter a lot.
Practise quick percentage sums.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (stopped after 45 seconds)
experiences.summary: 25 out of 40 passed. Without asking for an introduction, the officer asked why he wants to join and to speak on democracy and accountability, and stopped him after 45 seconds. Then came capitals, currencies, governors, chief ministers, percentage sums and bio data questions.
asked: Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Speak on democracy and accountability.
What is the capital of Greece? (and other important capitals and currencies)
Who are the Governors and Chief Ministers of the provinces?
Percentage maths questions.
Questions from the bio data form.
tips: Do not panic.
Answer with confidence and do not change your answer once given.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Captain-only interview
experiences.summary: Only a Captain took the whole interview, in a friendly way. He asked for an introduction, some geography and science GK, and about games and hobbies. He also asked why the candidate wants to join the Army. The friendly, smiling talk ended with 'Well done, you may go'.

Where is Nigeria and why is it famous?
Where is Egypt and why is it famous?
How many bones are there in the adult human body?
What are your games and hobbies?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
tips: Talk naturally and smile; treat it as a friendly conversation.
Work hard, pray and trust in Allah.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (asked to change topic)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'When I faced rejection' and 'Loneliness is the best companion'. After about an hour of waiting, the Colonel asked personal questions and why he wants the Army while studying at a university. He politely asked to change a speech topic he did not know, and spoke on 'Actions speak louder than words'.

Why do you want to join the Army even though you are at university?
Speak on a topic (changed to 'Actions speak louder than words').
What are the capitals of Germany and Ireland?

Write essays neatly with little cutting, in black or blue pen.
They need confidence more than strong GK.

experiences.title: PMA • Lahore AS&RC (repeater, round table)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Power of money' (English) and 'Bad effects of the internet on youth' (Urdu). A Lieutenant Colonel and a Major sat at a round table. The Colonel read his bio data silently for two minutes while he kept eye contact. He was asked about Gwadar and Balochistan's area, and the Major asked several times if he had any regret in life. Out of 60 boys, 25 were recommended.

In which year did Gwadar become part of Pakistan?
How much of Pakistan's area is Balochistan?
Are you a repeater? Did you appear in the Navy ISSB?
Do you have any regret in life? Has anyone hurt you?

Stay calm even when the officer is silent and reading your form.

experiences.title: PMA 154 • Karachi AS&RC (introduce in 4 lines)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Importance of tourism' and 'How can our society improve further' (Urdu). The Colonel asked his name and had a short friendly talk about it. He was asked to introduce himself in just 4 lines, then about his parents and joining PMA. The Major asked about his form, and they joked a little about his city. The interview was very general.

Introduce yourself in 4 lines.
Tell us about your parents.
Why do you want to join PMA?

Know your form well; they ask from it.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (very fast questions)

What are you doing nowadays?
Speak on co-education.

What is 3% of 1100?

experiences.summary: His essays were 'The role of students in educational awareness' (English) and 'Luck or hard work' (Urdu). A Major asked where he was from, what he was doing these days, and about FATF and how it works. He was given one minute to speak on population. He was then asked to find Australia on a map with a laser pointer, and the Major skipped it.
asked: Where are you from?
What are you doing these days?
What is FATF? How does it work?
Speak for 1 minute on population.
Do you know about maps? Find Australia on the map.

GK matters less than confidence.

experiences.title: PMA • Peshawar AS&RC (chemistry student)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Gender discrimination is a myth' (English) and 'Freedom of expression' (Urdu). The Colonel tested him by saying chemistry was a bad choice with no scope in the Army; he calmly explained other uses of chemistry. The psychologist asked him to point to Moscow on a map; he first said it is in Asia, then corrected himself.

When you entered, what did you say to ask permission?
What are you doing nowadays?
Why did you choose chemistry? It has no scope in the Army.
Point to Moscow on the world map. Which continent is it in?

In the essay, keep negative points few and always write a conclusion.

experiences.title: PMA • Two-minute speech on the education system

What is the capital of Bangladesh?
What is the currency of Turkey?
What are the full forms of UNICEF and CNG?
Who is the Governor of Punjab?
What is 4% of 700?

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Karachi centre
experiences.summary: He knocked, asked permission, and stood by the chair until told to sit. The board was a Colonel and a psychologist Major. After his introduction he was asked about the Indus Waters Treaty, which he explained in detail, and about the 1973 constitution. He was also asked about his strengths and weaknesses. The interview took about 9 minutes.
asked: Introduce yourself.
What is the Indus Waters Treaty?
Tell us about the constitution of Pakistan.
What is the 1973 constitution?
What are your strengths and weaknesses?

Prepare an honest list of your strengths and weaknesses.
Prepare national topics like the Indus Waters Treaty and the 1973 constitution.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Faisalabad centre
experiences.summary: A Colonel took a short interview. He asked the candidate to introduce himself and what he would do if he was not recommended. He then asked which game he plays and about the bad effects of video games and mobile phones. After that he let him go.
asked: Introduce yourself.
If we do not recommend you, what will you do?
Which game do you play?
What are the negative effects of video games?
What are the negative effects of mobile phones?
tips: Do not lose your confidence.
Greet with salam when you enter and leave, and say thank you.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Cricket player
experiences.summary: The interview was mostly a talk based on his interview form. After a short introduction he was asked about the Suez and Panama canals. Because he wrote cricket as his hobby, there was a long discussion on cricket records and the best team.
asked: Introduce yourself briefly.
Tell me about the Suez Canal and the Panama Canal.
Who is the highest run scorer in cricket?
Who is the highest wicket taker in cricket?
Which is the best cricket team in the world across all formats?
tips: Most questions come from your form, so prepare everything you write, especially hobbies and games.
Do not take pressure and stay confident.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (business vs job speech)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Slow and steady wins the race' and 'Difficulties in my life and my response'. He got only one GK answer right, but gave logical reasons in his speech on why business is better than a job, and was recommended.
asked: What is the capital of Iraq?
What is 5% of 500?
What is the motto of the Pakistan Army?
Who is the Chairman Joint Chiefs of Staff Committee?
Speak on why business is better than a job.
tips: Dress code and confidence are the main things.
Give logical points in your speech even if your GK answers are weak.

experiences.title: PMA 154 • Rawalpindi AS&RC (speech on social evils)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'The time I faced rejection' (English) and 'Loneliness is the best companion' (Urdu). He was asked what he was doing and why he wants to join the Army, and then gave a short speech on social evils. After that came quick GK, abbreviation and percentage questions.
asked: What are you doing nowadays?
Why do you want to join the Pakistan Army?
Give a speech on social evils.
What is the capital of the USA? What does DC stand for in Washington DC?
What does OGRA stand for?
What is 5% of 400?
tips: Practise quick percentage sums; they are asked often.

experiences.title: PMA • Faisalabad AS&RC (45-second introduction)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'My family' (Urdu) and 'Unforgettable incident of my life' (English). The Colonel gave him only 45 seconds to introduce himself, his hobbies and his siblings. He wrongly said Faisalabad is north of Sargodha, and the Colonel joked about the direction of the sun. The Colonel then pressed him on what he would do if not recommended and on his plan B; he said he had no plan B and would keep working hard.

In which direction is Faisalabad from Sargodha?
What are you doing nowadays?

What is your plan B?
tips: Prepare a short, complete introduction that fits in under a minute.
Know the directions and distances of the cities around your home district.

experiences.title: PMA • Rawalpindi AS&RC (gender inequality speech)
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Unpleasant event in my life' and 'One day in my life came when...'. He was asked quick GK questions, an abbreviation and a speech on gender inequality.
asked: What is the capital of Iraq?
What is the currency of Denmark?
Who is the President of Iran?
Who is the Chairman Senate?
What is the full form of NEPRA?
Speak on gender inequality.
tips: Revise capitals, currencies and current office holders; they are asked from almost everyone.

experiences.title: PMA • Asked about standing beside the chair
experiences.summary: His essays were 'Slow and steady wins the race' and 'Difficulties in my life and their solution'. The officer first asked why he stood on the right side of the chair, then gave speech topics and GK questions.
asked: Why are you standing on the right side of the chair?
Speak on the importance of western culture.
What is the capital of Bhutan?
Who is called Sher-e-Khuda?
What is 4% of 400?
Why do we need a single national curriculum in Pakistan?
tips: The officer notices small things like where you stand; be ready to explain calmly.
Prepare short speeches on common social topics.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Short interview (called by wrong name)
experiences.summary: A Colonel and a psychologist took the interview. The Colonel called him by a similar-sounding wrong name and he answered without noticing, which annoyed the Colonel a little. He calmly explained the mix-up. The psychologist said his Urdu was weak; they spoke Urdu and he answered confidently in English. The interview lasted about 2 minutes.
asked: What is your full name?
Your Urdu is very weak. Why?
Where did you complete your FSc?
tips: Listen carefully; if you did not hear clearly, politely ask them to repeat.
If you make a mistake, stay calm and explain briefly.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Bio data form questions
experiences.summary: After the physical test, candidates filled a bio data form for the interview. The form asked about the merits and demerits of himself, his parents, his best friend and his siblings. It also asked what his parents taught him, how he reacts to criticism and his biggest problem as a teenager. These answers are later used by the interviewers.
asked: What are your merits and demerits?
What are the good and bad qualities of your parents, best friend and siblings?
What have your parents taught you?
How do you respond when someone criticises you?
What was your biggest problem as a teenager?
tips: Think about honest answers on your own and your family's strengths and weaknesses before filling the form.
Keep your interview answers the same as what you wrote in the form.

experiences.title: PMA 153 • Peshawar centre
experiences.summary: His English essay was 'Honesty is the best policy' and his Urdu essay was 'My favourite personality'. He was asked how Pakistan can improve its relations with Iran and his height in inches. The other questions came from what he filled in his form.
asked: How can Pakistan improve its relationship with Iran?
What is your height in inches?
Questions from your form
tips: Know your exact height, weight and other personal details.
Remember everything you wrote in your form.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Multan centre
experiences.summary: His essays were on limited internet access for students (English) and unity of the Muslim Ummah (Urdu). He stood near the chair, said salam and sat when asked. A Captain asked him to introduce himself and asked only questions from his bio data form, with no GK. Out of 40 candidates, 18 passed.
asked: Introduce yourself.
Questions from your bio data form
tips: Know everything you wrote in your bio data form.
Still prepare GK, because other candidates were asked GK questions.

experiences.title: PMA • Officer did not return the salam
experiences.summary: His essays were 'The tragedy of poverty' (English) and 'My friends often...' (Urdu). The Colonel did not reply to his salam and only pointed to the chair. He asked a few quick GK questions and let him go.

Where is the Black Sea?
Who is the Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly?
Who is the Prime Minister of AJK?
tips: Do not be disturbed if the officer does not reply to your greeting; stay polite.

experiences.title: PMA 151 • Shortest interview

If a train moves at 33 km per hour, how far will it go in 3 hours?
What are your marks?
What will you do if you are not selected?

Have a calm, positive answer for 'what if you are not selected'.

experiences.title: PMA 152 • Peshawar centre (3-minute interview)
experiences.summary: He wrote two essays, one in English and one in Urdu. The interview lasted only about 3 minutes. He was asked where Mangla Dam is and two questions about the map of Pakistan. Only 7 out of 26 candidates in his group were recommended.

Speak for about one minute: your name, home area, education and marks, family in one line, hobbies, and end with why you want to join the Army. Keep it natural, not memorised word for word.
answers.What is the meaning of your name?: Find out the real meaning of your name before the interview and say it in one short line. If it is linked to a famous person or quality, you may mention that.
answers.How do you pronounce your name?: Say your full name slowly and clearly, the same way it is written in your documents.
answers.What are you doing these days?: Tell the truth: your current studies or work, plus how you are preparing for the Army (fitness, reading, GK). Show that you are using your time well.
Know your district's location, main cities, rivers, famous places, main crops or industry, and any current issue there. Speak about it with pride but honestly.
answers.Why do you want to join the Pakistan Arm: Give a personal, honest reason like serving the country, a life of discipline and leadership, or inspiration from a real person you know. Avoid only saying 'for the uniform' or 'for the salary'.
answers.Why did you choose the Pak Army when the: Explain that the Army is not just a job for you but a way of life with service, honour and leadership. Link it to something real from your own life.
answers.What will you do if you are not recommen: Stay calm and positive: say you will find your mistakes, improve, and apply again in the next course, while continuing your studies.
answers.What is your plan B?: Give a real, sensible backup like completing your degree in your field, but make it clear the Army is your first choice and you will try again.
answers.What are your strengths and weaknesses?: Give 2-3 real strengths with a short example each. For weaknesses, give a real but not serious one and say what you are doing to fix it.
answers.How do you respond when someone criticis: Say you listen calmly, think about whether it is right, and use it to improve. Give a small real example if you can.
answers.What was your biggest problem as a teena: Mention a real, normal problem (like time management, shyness or a study difficulty) and explain how you handled it and what you learned.
answers.You were a house prefect. Tell me about: Explain what duties you had, one problem you solved, and how you treated the people under you. Only claim roles you really had.
answers.What big thing do you want to do for you: Give a simple, realistic aim, like being a good officer who serves with honesty, supports your family and helps people of your area. Avoid big empty promises.
answers.What is your height in inches?: Know your exact height and weight in both feet-inches and centimetres before the interview, and answer quickly.
answers.Do you tell lies?: Answer honestly and calmly. You can admit you are human, but say you value truth and try your best to always be honest.
answers.Can you explain what you wrote in your b: Read your form copy again before the interview. Every answer you give should match what you wrote there.
answers.How do you think your interview went?: Answer briefly and politely, for example that you tried your best and learned something. Do not argue or sound overconfident.
answers.What does your father do?: Say his profession clearly and respectfully, whatever it is. Be ready to explain a little about his work and what you learned from him.
answers.Do you have siblings? What are their nam: Give each sibling's name, age order and what they study or do in one short line each.
answers.What have your parents taught you?: Mention 2-3 real values like honesty, respect and hard work, with a small example from your life.
answers.What are the good and bad qualities of y: Speak respectfully. Mention real good qualities first, and for the bad side keep it mild and fair, such as being very strict out of care.

answers.Your grades are low. Why?: Accept it honestly and do not blame your school, teachers or anyone else. Say what caused it and what you are doing now to improve.
answers.You got good marks in FSc pre-medical, s: Explain honestly that the Army is your real interest and first choice. Do not speak badly of other careers.
answers.How many times have you applied to the a: Tell the exact number truthfully. If you applied many times, show it as determination and say what you improved each time.
answers.Why were you not recommended in your las: Be honest about what went wrong (for example nervousness or weak GK) and clearly say what you have improved since then.
answers.Why did you change your test centre?: Give the real reason in one line, such as moving for studies or family. Keep it simple and truthful.

Before the interview: The initial interview is the last step at the selection centre, after the computer test, physical and medical; clearing it sends you to the ISSB. Many candidates fail here, so start preparing right after the test.
Fill the bio data form honestly and remember every answer, including hobbies, fears and weaknesses, because the officers ask questions from it.
Prepare a clear self-introduction of under one minute (name, area, studies, family, hobbies, reason for joining), and also a 4-line short version.
Know the meaning of your name and have a real, personal reason for joining the Army.
Know your exact personal details: height in inches, weight, age, marks, and why any marks are low.
Know your family well: parents' and siblings' jobs, your father's rank and unit if he served, and step-family if you have one.
Know your hobbies, sports and the subject you are studying now in detail; choose sensible hobbies, not things like 'internet scrolling'.
Know your own district: its tehsils, rivers, mountain ranges, motorways and the direction of nearby cities.
Learn current office holders (President, PM, Chief Ministers, Governors, Chairman Senate, NA Speaker, CJCSC, world leaders), world capitals and currencies.
Learn common full forms (CNG, NEPRA, OGRA, PEMRA, FATF, UNICEF, JCO, AFIC), the Army motto, Army ranks and military awards.
Practise reading the map of Pakistan and the world map: continents, major countries, seas, dams and rivers.
Revise basic GK: Pakistan's history and key dates, constitutions, Pakistan-India wars and Islamic history.
Follow current news, including your home area, Pakistan's economy, world conflicts and big sports events.
Dress formally: light full-sleeve shirt with sleeves down, dark dress pants, formal lace-up shoes and neat hair; no jeans or loafers. Make sure your form photo matches how you look now.

Take your original certificates, CNIC (or B-form with a parent's CNIC if under 18), attested copies and colour photos; repeaters also bring their ISSB 'Not Recommended' letter. Expect to wait many hours.
In the room: Knock, ask 'May I come in, sir?' (say 'sir/madam' if a lady officer is present), close the door gently and greet the whole panel with salam.
Stand beside the chair and sit only when told; say thank you.
Sit straight, do not cross your legs or lock your hands, and keep your hands and feet still.
Keep eye contact and a natural smile throughout, even when the officer is silently reading your form.
Speak in a clear, loud and steady voice; most of the interview is in English, so avoid mixing Urdu words.
The board is usually a Colonel or Lt Col with a psychologist Major or a Captain; respect all of them equally.
Sometimes only the psychologist (often a lady officer) takes the interview; she may only watch and take notes, so behave well the whole time.
Do not be disturbed if an officer does not reply to your salam or looks at you closely; stay polite and calm.
The interview is short (often 2-10 minutes), so your first impression matters a lot.
When leaving, stand up, thank the panel, say salam to both officers and walk out calmly.
Answering: Confidence and the way you speak matter more than knowing every answer; many were recommended after answering only a few GK questions.
If you do not know an answer, say 'Sorry sir, I don't know' calmly with eye contact; one sorry is not rejection, but avoid many.
Do not guess wildly or make up answers, and once you give an answer, do not keep changing it.
Answer personal and honesty questions truthfully and calmly.
Be honest about weak marks, repeated attempts or past failures, never blame others, and say what you have improved.
Listen carefully; many candidates say sorry to easy questions only because they did not listen. If you did not hear, politely ask the officer to repeat.
Think for 2-3 seconds before answering, then give a full answer; very short answers make a weak impression.
If you are weak in one area, say so honestly and offer your strong subject.
Expect deep questions from the subject you study now or got high marks in.
Prepare 1-2 minute talks on common topics: co-education, education system, globalization, gender equality, religious harmony, tourism, population, democracy and social evils.
When given a topic, start with your main point and keep speaking until they stop you; if you do not know the topic, politely ask to change it.
Practise quick mental maths: 60 km/h is 1 km per minute; zakat is the amount divided by 40; poles = length / gap + 1; and percentages like 3% of 500.
Be ready for estimation questions, like distance, time or the size of a table.
The officer may pressure you or criticise your choices on purpose; stay calm, polite and do not argue.
Be ready for the interview to switch suddenly from Urdu to English.
Essay: You write one English and one Urdu essay before the interview, about 5-10 minutes and 12-15 lines each, worth about 20 marks in total; practise both with a timer.
Spend 1-2 minutes on a quick outline, then write: introduction, 2-3 main points and a clear conclusion.
Write the topic in the centre at the top, use short clear sentences, neat handwriting, black or blue pen and little cutting.
One essay is often about your own life (happiest, saddest or unforgettable moment, a rejection, your aim); prepare a few real events in advance.
Be truthful in life-event essays, because the officers may ask about them; write your feelings and how the event changed you.
On debate topics, give both sides first and then your own balanced opinion.
Keep negative points few, stay positive and always end with a conclusion.
Add one famous quote or a simple fact to make the essay stronger.
Learn a few good words with their meanings and use them correctly.
General topics come from social and religious issues, current affairs and Pakistan's problems, so read about them.
Practise 4-5 essays with a timer and show them to a teacher or family member for feedback.
